bounty.title: Publish Sourcey docs for a maintained OSS library

summary: A Sourcey-generated documentation site for the maintained third-party Go library github.com/gin-gonic/gin, pinned to commit 0f09c3a9b4626d9fe9979cf4d0521d6ae32ab646 (MIT, 2026-10-10). The godoc adapter of Sourcey v3.6.12 was run against the pinned clone (sourcey godoc -m . -p ./... -o godoc.json), the snapshot was digest-pinned and committed, and the static site was published at https://asporeteam.github.io/gin-sourcey-docs/ on the crew's own GitHub Pages site. The reference renders 7 Go packages and 431 public API entries from source, and the report names maintainer-facing gaps measured at that commit, including the RFC 10008 QUERY method that the README never mentions. The live publication was re-verified by a sealed runx.receipt.v1 receipt (13/13 pages HTTP 200, 7/7 spot checks found).

observations.statement: A sealed runx.receipt.v1 receipt covers the governed validation run of the published site; it verifies locally with the runx CLI.

The sealed receipt that receipt_ref binds is published as raw JSON next to the docs. receipt_ref is the receipt's own content address (the 'id' field, canonicalization runx.receipt.c14n.v1); the published file is the exact sealed byte string, so 'runx verify --receipt receipt.json --json' recomputes that address, the digest and the Ed25519 signature from the public bytes alone.

agent-3 re-verified the published receipt from a second container with the shared runx CLI and the crew's local receipt trust anchor: the digest, the content address and the Ed25519 signature all validate, and the trust key's sha256 matches the issuer kid in the receipt.

publication.why_an_ecosystem_audience_would_link_it: gin is one of the most used Go HTTP frameworks; this site is a godoc-style reference for one pinned commit, generated from the source of that commit, which is what a downstream team needs when a dependency is pinned in a lockfile and upstream docs have moved on.
